additional_claims.claim_text: Overall, the offering is a high-risk, subordinated, non-voting SAFE in an operating but loss-making company with a going-concern paragraph, an arbitrary cap equal to 2022 investors' cap, and unverified traction claims. The pack lacks evidence on availability, investor-side fees, the final contract and interim results. This is a research observation, not a decision.

business_model.assessment: Mightylicious is an operating consumer-packaged-food company, not pre-revenue. It sells gluten-free cookies, flour blends and brownie mix through grocery retail, wholesale, its own website and Amazon-type channels [A29]. Revenue grew about 32% in FY2025 to $459,216 [A19][A21], but cost of goods sold was higher than revenue, so the gross result was negative [A22][B3]. Advertising and promotion was about 93% of revenue [B5]. The model has not yet shown unit economics that work at current scale. The issuer says it plans vertical integration to cut COGS [B10], but no plan, cost or timeline is in the pack. Reviewed statements, going-concern paragraph and 2 employees are further context [A25][A26][A34].

competition.assessment: The issuer names Aliea's, Tate's Bake Shop, Dr. Schar and Udi's as key competitors [A30], and its risk factors say competitors have far greater resources and that retailers can demand discounts and allowances for shelf space. No market size, share or independent comparison is in the pack. Differentiation is asserted (taste, vegan/kosher/non-GMO, awards in a press release) and not independently corroborated. Trademarks are registered [A30], but the pack shows no other moat. The competitive position is unknown.

demand_evidence.assessment: Documented demand evidence is reviewed FY2025 revenue growth ($347,602 to $459,216) [A19][A21] and a 2022 Republic raise of about $5M from 4,365 investors, which is an issuer statement consistent with SAFE principal on the balance sheet [A32][A17]. Retail traction claims (1,800 doors, Kroger/Giant/HEB/HyVee, '$100K MoM run rate', Amazon +355% YoY) appear only in an undated testing-the-waters email [A31]. They are unverified and lack a defined period or basis. A $100K monthly run rate would be about $1.2M annualized, far above FY2025 revenue, so it may include gross or peak figures or something else. The pack has no interim financials, sales reports, retailer contracts, channel split or repeat-purchase data. Demand is therefore only partly supported, and the growth could be driven by paid promotion [B5].

economics_and_funding.assessment: FY2025 (ended Dec 31, 2025, not stale): revenue $459,216, COGS $488,693, net loss $896,217 versus $622,749 in FY2024 [A19][A20][A23]. Cash at year end was $116,414, plus $1,397,792 of marketable securities that fell from $2,302,274 [A24]. Withdrawals from that portfolio of about $758,853 in 2025 funded operations [B6]. The reviewers added a going-concern paragraph [A25]. The June 30, 2026 cash of $654,000 and '5 months runway' is an unsupported issuer claim on a different basis from the Dec 2025 cash, so no runway is computed here [A27]. The CEO's email says the higher run rate has 'accelerated our cash burn' [B7]. SAFE principal of about $5.1M sits as a liability against $1.85M total assets and a $3.5M stockholders' deficit [B4][A17]. Other debt is small: EIDL $80,000, Wayflyer $51,000, CEO loans $8,475 [A28]. The maximum raise of $1M is about 1.1 times FY2025 net loss [B2], and at the $75,000 target fees alone take about 23% [B1]. Proceeds are mainly marketing and launch inventory [A35], and the press release adds vertical integration and executive hires without budget lines [B10]. The company will likely need more capital soon.

execution_risks.assessment: Main risks are: (1) negative gross margin with heavy marketing spend [B3][B5]; (2) going-concern doubt and dependence on further financing [A25]; (3) a two-person team with the founder handling sales, operations and admin [A34][A35]; (4) retail concentration, shelf-space pressure and supply-chain dependence on third parties; (5) possible securities-law compliance issues in testing-the-waters communications and prior offerings, with rescission risk [A36]; (6) inconsistencies in the filing that lower reliability: HQ New Jersey versus New York [A39], custodian entity names [A13], conflicting SAFE conversion descriptions [A37][A38], and notes that describe customers who 'prepay for services at the time of booking', which looks like template text [B11]; (7) reviewed-only financials [A26]. Planned launches at Wakefern and Wegmans are claims for Q4 2026 and not documented [A31].

price_and_terms.assessment: Price terms are analyzed separately from business quality. The price is $1.00 per unit, 'Arbitrary', and the filing says it bears no relation to value [A4][A7]. The cap is $15M pre-money, which is about 32.7 times FY2025 revenue [B8], and the same cap applies to the roughly $5.1M of SAFEs issued earlier [A17]. No discount, early-bird tier or investor-favorable term was found [A7][A8]. The cap is calculated before counting SAFEs, so earlier and new SAFEs do not reduce the share count used for the cap price and later holders can be diluted more than a headline cap suggests. Existing SAFE principal is about 34% of the cap amount [B9]. The Form C's 25.36% ownership figure for existing SAFEs appears to use a different basis, which I did not reconcile [A17]. The intermediary also gets 1.5% in securities, which adds to the total outstanding [A16]. Fees are issuer-paid [A15], while BitGo custody account fees are blank in the pack, so investor-side costs are unknown [A13]. A custody account is mandatory and the SAFE is void without the nominee agreement [A13]. There are no information rights beyond the annual report and no anti-dilution [A12]. The SAFE form is an unsigned template [A8]. Governance gives the CEO sole power to amend it [A12]. Availability is unconfirmed; the deadline is 12-18-2026, but a deadline is not evidence of an open offering [A5]. Minimum $100, maximum $124,000, changeable at issuer discretion [A6].

security_path_to_proceeds.assessment: This is a SAFE, not equity or debt, and it has no interest, maturity, dividend or repurchase right [A3][A14]. Cash could come in three ways. (1) Conversion: on an Equity Financing of at least $1,000,000 in cash, the SAFE converts into that round's shares at the cap-based price or the lowest round price [A8][A9]. That gives shares, not cash, in a still-illiquid private company. (2) A Liquidity Event (sale, IPO, direct listing): the holder gets the greater of the purchase amount or the as-converted amount, but only from available funds and behind debt and creditors, on par with other SAFEs and preferred [A11]. (3) Dissolution: same priority, with SAFE holders ahead of common only. The company already has about $5.1M of SAFEs that rank equally, and the balance sheet shows total assets of $1.85M [B4][A17]. In a failure, little would remain after creditors. What usually prevents payout: no equity round happens, the company stays private or fails, or a sale price is too low to cover all SAFE holders. The issuer 'may never' do an equity financing or liquidity event [A40]. Conversion wording conflicts: a risk factor says the issuer has discretion, while SAFE s.1(a) says it 'shall' issue shares [A37]. The notes describe a different, investor-election model [A38]. Investors hold only a beneficial interest through a custodian, have no voting or information rights, and the CEO alone can amend the SAFE [A12][A13]. Transfers are restricted and no secondary market exists [A40].

team_evidence.assessment: Only one person is documented: founder/CEO Carolyn Haeler. Her documented background is finance and supply-chain consulting (J.P. Morgan asset management, a hedge fund, IBM) and an MBA, and since 2017 she has built the brand to Whole Foods placement by January 2018, per the issuer's own bio [A33]. That shows execution history in getting a product on shelves over several years. No food-manufacturing or CPG operating executives are listed, advisors are unnamed, and the Form C says she handles a wide range of admin and operational functions with 2 employees [A34][A35]. She owns all common stock and controls the company [A18]. The press release says key executive hires are planned [B10].

briefing_ko.failure_reasons: 첫째, 2025년 매출원가가 매출의 약 106%라 팔수록 손해인 구조입니다 [B3]. 둘째, 영업활동 현금유출이 960,595달러였고 계속기업 불확실성 문구가 있습니다 [C3][A25]. 셋째, 최대 모집액 100만 달러는 2025년 영업현금유출 규모와 비슷해 오래 버티기 어렵고 추가 자금조달이 필요할 가능성이 큽니다 [C4]. 넷째, 1,800개 매장, 월 10만 달러 매출 같은 성과는 날짜와 기준이 없는 마케팅 이메일에만 있고 2025년 매출과 맞지 않습니다 [A31]. 다섯째, 문서에 다른 업종 같은 문구, 본사 위치 불일치, 부채 수치 차이가 있어 자료 신뢰도가 떨어집니다 [B11][C12][A39][C13].
briefing_ko.future_evidence: 긍정적으로 바뀔 증거: 플랫폼에서 확인된 모집 상태, 중간 재무제표에서 매출총이익 흑자 전환, 소매업체 계약·판매 보고서로 입증된 매출, 수수료가 확정된 최종 계약서에서 전환·수탁 조항 충돌이 해소된 것, 신규 투자 유치 조건 공개. 부정적으로 바뀔 증거: 2026년 연차보고서(Form C-AR)에서 매출 정체 또는 현금 급감, 계속기업 문구 유지, 신규 부채 또는 불리한 조건의 추가 SAFE 발행. 이 내용은 투자 결정이 아닌 검토 우선순위 판단용입니다.
briefing_ko.investor_proceeds_path: SAFE는 이자·만기·배당이 없습니다 [A3][A14]. 돈이 되는 경로는 세 가지입니다. (1) 100만 달러 이상 현금을 모으는 다음 지분 투자 유치 때 그 라운드 주식으로 전환되는데, 이는 현금이 아니라 거래 불가능한 비상장 주식입니다 [A8][A9]. (2) 회사 매각·상장 때 원금과 전환가치 중 큰 금액을 받지만 가용 자금 한도 안에서이고 부채보다 후순위입니다 [A11]. (3) 해산 때도 채권자 뒤, 다른 SAFE와 동순위입니다 [A11]. 회사가 지분 투자 유치나 매각을 영영 하지 않을 수 있으며 그러면 계속 보유해야 하고 거래할 시장도 없습니다 [A40]. 기존 SAFE 약 510만 달러가 같은 순위로 있고 총자산은 약 185만 달러입니다 [A17][B4].
briefing_ko.price_and_contract: 가격은 '임의(Arbitrary)'로 정해졌고 1,500만 달러 상한은 2025년 매출의 약 32.7배입니다 [A4][A7][B8]. 할인율이 없고, 상한 계산에서 모든 SAFE가 제외되어 기존·신규 SAFE가 함께 전환되면 실제 지분율이 표면 비율보다 낮아집니다 (전액 모집 시 약 4.7% 대 단순 6.7%, 예시 계산) [A10][C11]. 의결권·정보열람권이 없고 CEO가 대리인이며 CEO만 계약 조항을 바꿀 수 있습니다 [A12]. 수탁기관 계좌가 필수이고 그 약관이 SAFE와 충돌하면 우선하며, 수수료표는 비어 있고 수탁기관 이름도 문서마다 다릅니다 [A13][C2]. 전환이 '의무'인지 '회사 재량'인지도 문서마다 다릅니다 [A37][A38]. 중개사 수수료는 회사가 내지만 증권 1.5%도 받습니다 [A15][A16]. 최소 투자액은 100달러입니다 [A6].
briefing_ko.strongest_evidence: 검토를 거친 재무제표상 2025년 매출은 347,602달러에서 459,216달러로 늘었습니다 [A19][A21]. 매출총손실은 약 -117K달러에서 약 -29K달러로 줄었고, 광고비 비중도 매출의 약 125%에서 약 93%로 낮아졌습니다 [C9][C7]. 2022년에 약 500만 달러를 모았다는 발표는 대차대조표의 SAFE 원금과 대체로 맞습니다 [A32][A17]. 다만 이 자료는 모두 회사가 만든 것이고 재무제표도 감사가 아닌 검토 수준입니다 [A26].
briefing_ko.summary: Mightylicious는 글루텐 프리 쿠키·가루·브라우니 믹스를 파는 실제 매출이 있는 회사로, 이번에 전환 가능 증권(SAFE)을 최대 100만 달러까지 모집합니다 [A3][A4]. 2025년 매출은 459,216달러로 약 32% 늘었지만 매출원가가 매출보다 커서 순손실이 896,217달러였고, 검토 보고서에 계속기업 불확실성 문구가 있습니다 [A19][A21][A23][A25]. 기업가치 상한은 1,500만 달러로 임의로 정해졌고, 기존 SAFE 약 510만 달러도 같은 상한을 갖습니다 [A7][A17]. 투자 가능 여부와 투자자 쪽 수수료 같은 핵심 정보가 자료에 없어, 이 노트는 검토할 가치가 있는지 판단하는 참고용이며 투자 조언이 아닙니다 [A5].
briefing_ko.unknowns: 모집이 현재 열려 있는지와 모금액 [A5][C1], 투자자가 부담할 수탁 수수료 [C2], 최종 서명본 SAFE, 2025년 12월 이후 재무제표와 6월 30일 현금 654,000달러·5개월 런웨이의 근거 [A27], 전체 지분 구조와 옵션풀, 병행 사모 조달 조건 [C14], 매장·매출 주장의 증빙, 채널별 매출과 원가 구조, 수직계열화 비용 계획 [B10]은 알 수 없습니다. 일부 첨부(Exhibit E)는 텍스트가 비어 있습니다.
briefing_ko.what_it_does: 뉴저지 기반 회사로 쿠키, 가루 믹스, 브라우니 믹스를 슈퍼마켓·도매·자사 웹사이트(소비자 직접 판매)로 팝니다. 돈을 내는 쪽은 소매업체와 일반 소비자입니다 [A29]. 경쟁사로는 Tate's Bake Shop, Dr. Schar, Udi's 등을 듭니다 [A30]. 직원은 2명이고 창업자 겸 CEO가 영업·운영을 맡습니다 [A34]. 채널별 매출과 시장 규모 자료는 자료에 없습니다.

forecasts.outcome_definition: A Form C-AR for fiscal year 2026 is filed on EDGAR by Mightylicious Inc by 2027-10-14 and reports FY2026 revenue above $459,216 (the FY2025 figure).
forecasts.probability_basis: Judgment only. FY2025 revenue grew about 32% (A21) and the CEO email claims higher run rates and new retail chains, but that is an unverified claim (A31). Offsetting this, the company has a negative gross margin, a going-concern paragraph and about five months of stated runway (A22, A25, A27), so a funding gap or a missed filing could prevent a report. Reporting lag is long because the Form C-AR is due about 120 days after fiscal year end.
forecasts.resolution_evidence: Form C-AR on SEC EDGAR for Mightylicious Inc, revenue line for fiscal year 2026 (or the Form C-AR XML revenue field).
forecasts.unknown_treatment: If no Form C-AR is on EDGAR by the resolution date plus the lag, the outcome is recorded as 'unresolved/not observed', not as the event failing. Only a filed report showing revenue at or below $459,216 resolves it as not occurring.

forecasts.outcome_definition: Mightylicious Inc files a new Form C or Form D (a new capital raise, excluding amendments of the current Form C) with the SEC between 2026-10-15 and 2027-04-14.
forecasts.probability_basis: Judgment only. The company reports limited runway and a going-concern paragraph (A25, A27) and permits concurrent private raises (C14), which raise the chance of another filing. The current offering runs to 12-18-2026 with a $1M maximum (A4), which could provide funds and make a new raise less likely within six months. Private raises under other exemptions may not be filed or may not be visible, so the probability is modest.
forecasts.resolution_evidence: SEC EDGAR filing index for Mightylicious Inc (CIK 0002147043) showing a Form C or Form D with a filing date in the window.
forecasts.unknown_treatment: If EDGAR cannot be checked, the outcome is recorded as unknown. Absence of a visible filing after the 15-day lag counts as the event not observed, while private raises that are never filed are not counted either way.

The operative contract is an unsigned template. It conflicts with the risk factor and the financial statement notes (A37, A38). The custodian entity is named inconsistently (A13). Custody Account Agreement terms override the SAFE (C2). Template-like text in the Form C and the notes lowers reliability (B11, C12). There are no interim financials (A27) and the Wayflyer debt figures differ between documents (C13). The gate therefore cannot pass. Most identity and FY2025 financial facts are cited, but they come from the issuer's own filing.

Unit economics and path to margin
Team execution history documented in the pack
gates.uncertainty: Reviewed revenue grew about 32% in FY2025, the gross loss narrowed from about -$117K to about -$29K, and advertising intensity fell (A21, C9, C7). Against this, gross margin is still negative, the net loss widened to $896K, and the reviewers added a going-concern paragraph (A22, A23, A25). Traction claims (1,800 doors, '$100K MoM run rate', retailer wins) sit only in an undated marketing email and conflict with FY2025 revenue (A31). The $654K June 2026 cash and 5-month runway are unsupported (A27). The vertical-integration plan has no cost or timeline (B10). The team is one documented officer plus one other employee, and her record rests on her own bio (A33, A34). The documents do not allow a positive or negative conclusion. Interim sales data, channel split and gross margin drivers would be decisive.

criteria_applied: Price and cap supported by objective criteria
Investor-favorable terms (discount, tiering, information rights, voting)
Operative contract is clear, final and internally consistent
Dilution and seniority consequences for a new holder
gates.uncertainty: The $15M pre-money cap is arbitrary and is about 32.7 times FY2025 revenue (A4, A7, B8). There is no discount or early-bird tier (A8). The cap math excludes all SAFEs, and about $5.1M of earlier SAFEs sit at the same cap, so a new holder's post-conversion share is well below the headline ratio (A10, A17, C11). The SAFE is junior to debt and ranks equally with the other SAFEs (A11). The CEO alone can amend the SAFE, there are no information or voting rights, and the CEO acts as proxy (A12). The Custody Account Agreement overrides the SAFE, its fees are blank, and the custodian entity is inconsistent (A13, C2). Conversion wording conflicts (mandatory 'shall' vs issuer discretion), and the notes describe a different model (A37, A38). The intermediary also receives 1.5% in securities (A16), and concurrent private raises are possible with undisclosed terms (C14). In the investor's favor: the SAFE has a liquidation floor at the purchase amount if funds are available, and the issuer cannot repurchase it (A11, A14). The terms are not shown to be good for a new investor. The 'fail' reflects absent investor-favorable terms and unresolved contract conflicts. The final executed SAFE could change this.

assumptions.other: Illustrative $1,000 purchase. Assumes the full $1M is raised and all SAFEs (about $5.1M existing, $1M new) convert at the $15M cap, so the holder's share is 1,000 / (15,000,000 + 5,096,791 + 1,000,000) = about 0.00474%. Assumes 30% further dilution before exit, and treats $30M as equity value available to all holders, ignoring debt, liquidation preferences, the option pool, the 1.5% intermediary securities and fees. Not a forecast.

scenario.explanation_ko: 가정: 1,000달러 투자, 100만 달러 전액 모집, 기존 SAFE 약 510만 달러와 신규 SAFE가 모두 상한 가격으로 전환, 이후 지분 30% 추가 희석, 5년 뒤 기업가치 3,000만 달러에 매각. 이 경우 지분율은 약 0.00474%에서 약 0.00332%로 줄고 지분 가치는 약 995달러로 원금 수준입니다 (계산: 1,000/21,096,791×0.7×30,000,000). 부채, 우선권, 옵션풀, 수탁 비용은 무시한 단순 예시입니다. 매각가가 낮거나 SAFE 전환이 일어나지 않거나 회사가 실패하면 결과는 더 나쁠 수 있습니다. 이는 기대 수익이 아니라 구조를 이해하기 위한 예시입니다 [A10][A17][C11].
